title: Exchange: custom retention periods for message trace data
summary: The briefing correctly distinguishes the planned retention choice from Microsoft's currently documented fixed 90-day retention. The search command, permissions and Exchange Online entitlement are supported; the search path only omits a section heading.

claims.where: Risk assessment; controls[1].governs; Governance controls
claims.claim: Today's message trace search window covers the last 90 days.
claims.quote: You can search for message data within this 90-day window using either the Exchange admin center (modern EAC) or Exchange Online PowerShell cmdlets like Get-MessageTraceV2 and Start-HistoricalSearch.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Get-MessageTraceV2 returns at most 10 days of data per query.
claims.quote: You can only return 10 days worth of data per query.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Investigations cannot rely on message trace to retrieve data older than the current 90-day retention window.
claims.quote: After 90 days, message trace data is automatically purged from the system.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Message trace is an administrator troubleshooting tool that reports whether messages were received, rejected, deferred or delivered.
claims.quote: The message trace feature lets you, as an administrator, follow email messages as they pass through your Exchange Online service. It helps you determine whether a targeted email message was received, rejected, deferred, or delivered by the service.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: The listed trace search reads message trace information rather than changing retention.
claims.quote: This retention period is not configurable. After 90 days, message trace data is automatically purged from the system. You can search for message data within this 90-day window

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The roadmap description specifies no automated action.
claims.quote: We will be introducing customizable retention options for Message Trace logs. Organizations will be able to choose from a predefined set of retention periods.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Scope; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The Exchange admin center search route is Mail flow > Message trace > Start a trace > New message trace > Search.
claims.quote: go to Mail flow > Message trace. ... selecting Start a trace. ... In the New message trace flyout that opens ... Report type ... Select Search to start the message trace.
claims.fix: Include the documented section heading in controls[1].ui.path and the rendered table: 'Mail flow > Message trace > Start a trace > New message trace > Report type > Search'. The cited page places Search under Report type; every printed step is otherwise correct.
